segments.text: Newton's second law: the net force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration. Resolve forces along the direction of motion before applying it.
Kinetic friction is modelled as the coefficient of kinetic friction times the normal force, and it always opposes the relative motion.

cases.question: A 3 kg block is pushed with 12 N while friction acts. How do I get its acceleration?
cases.reply: {"answer":"Subtract friction from the push to get the net force, then divide by the mass.","working":"Newton's second law gives a = F_net / m; the forces must be resolved along the direction of motion first [lecture-4.pdf p.1].","confidence":0.91,"why":"The method is the second law applied along the surface.","sayThis":"Work out the net force along the surface, then divide by the mass."}

cases.question: How is kinetic friction written, and which way does it point?
cases.reply: {"answer":"As the coefficient of kinetic friction times the normal force, pointing against the relative motion.","working":"That is the model used throughout the problems, so the sign is always opposite the sliding direction [lecture-4.pdf p.3].","confidence":0.89,"why":"Given as the friction model in the handout.","sayThis":"Mu-k times the normal force, always opposing the sliding."}
